title: Non-atomic StateDB commit
summary: StateDB.Commit persists dirty accounts one at a time in lexicographic address order without rolling back earlier writes if a later one fails; the x/erc20 IBC refund callback swallows the resulting error so partial writes persist. An attacker can create a credit without a matching debit, producing spendable native balance. Fix stages writes in a scratch cache context and publishes them only after all writes succeed.

title: Balance underflow in EVM StateDB
summary: The EVM StateDB tracks only an account's spendable balance. When a vesting account delegates more than its spendable balance through the staking precompile, the balance write-back subtracts the full amount without a check, an unchecked underflow that wraps the account balance to ~2^256. Chained with a second overflow on a victim account in a supply-neutral transaction, attackers extracted legitimate tokens (theft of funds) from six Cosmos EVM chains in Aug 2026 (~USD 5.7M). The fix adds an underflow guard; state-breaking, requires a coordinated upgrade.

title: CWA-2026-006: Sandbox escape in the Wasmer Singlepass compiler
summary: A code generation defect in the Wasmer Singlepass compiler, which wasmvm embeds to execute CosmWasm contracts, allows a specially crafted contract to escape the WebAssembly execution boundary and run controlled native instructions inside the node process. On an affected chain this permits unauthorized minting of native tokens and permanent loss of user funds. Exploitation requires an attacker to store and instantiate a contract they control. title: CWA-2026-005: Large number of locals in Wasm functions may stall the chain

title: CWA-2025-007: Unbounded reply recursion causing stack overflow
summary: A flaw in the reply handling logic allowed a contract to recursively trigger submessages from within its own reply handler without proper depth limitation. This could lead to unbounded recursion and eventually a stack overflow in the wasmd process, causing the node to crash. The issue does not directly lead to fund loss, but under certain conditions it could result in validator crashes and potential chain halt.

title: CWA-2024-002: CosmWasm affected by arithmetic overflows
summary: Some mathematical operations in cosmwasm-std use wrapping math instead of panicking on overflow for very big numbers. The only value that can overflow is Int{256,512}::MIN . Affected if overflow-checks = true is not set: - Uint{64,128}::pow / Int{64,128}::pow - Int{64,128}::neg (the unary negation operator - ). The only value that can overflow is Int{64,128}::MIN .

title: CWA-2023-001: Potential overflow in cache statistics
summary: By using unchecked increments in cache statistics it is possible to trigger an overflow after ~4 billion calls. Since cosmwasm-vm is compiled with overflow-checks = true in wasmvm, exceeding the uint32 range will lead to panics. For nodes that are accessible by clients, this can happen in case of excessive external calls. For nodes that only have cache hits as part of block production, it is unclear if the required numbers of calls can be reached. It might be possible for pinned contracts which have 0 instantiation cost by default.
